originalTitle: I Need You to Break Open My Heart: The Story of China's First Experimental Film Group
overview: From the Cultural Revolution to Reform and Opening, from June 1989 to contemporary China, the intertwined lives and careers of Shi Jian, Wang Zijun, Chen Jue, and Kuang Yang illuminate a country repeatedly remaking itself. In 1989, they formed Structure • Wave • Youth • Cinema, China's first experimental film group. Their central work, the eight-part Tiananmen, transformed Beijing into a laboratory for rethinking images, history, and everyday life. Through candid interviews, film excerpts, and archival footage, this documentary traces forty years of friendship and collaboration. Working largely inside state institutions, SWYC reshaped how ordinary people appeared on screen. Yet their achievements coexist with unfinished films and unseen histories. An intimate collective portrait becomes a history of modern China, asking what a nation loses when it cannot confront, record, and learn from its own past.
title: I Need You to Break Open My Heart: The Story of China's First Experimental Film Group
